output.methodChoice: D (competing hypotheses): several rival explanations with clear discriminating evidence already in the initial data.
output.brief: The August drop is almost entirely explained by the east-riser chiller (CH-2) failure from 4 to 19 August. It left floors 6-8 at 26-29 C for about two weeks. Floors 6-8 room comfort fell from 8.4 to 6.1, and their overall score fell from 8.6 to 7.4. Scores recovered to 8.4 once cooling was restored. Floors 1-5 were flat. 56 of the 74 negative comments were about heat, all from floors 6-8. Cleanliness scores, inspection pass rates and kiosk metrics did not move, so neither Orrin nor the kiosks is implicated. Don't serve notice on Orrin and don't pull the kiosks. The survey questionnaire was unchanged. The 6% rate rise may have nudged value-for-money scores down on floors 1-5, but that is not separable from the usual August dip, so leave rates alone and keep watching. Next steps: reinstate the deferred maintenance on both chillers, stock critical spares, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. A return-stay offer for affected guests is reasonable. They already received an apology and a half-night credit. Report August as it is; don't exclude the floors 6-8 responses. I'm fairly confident, and I collected no further evidence because more would be unlikely to change these actions.
